title: jXchange Master, format 2
description: One generated file per jXchange TPG Master: its operations, their request and response element trees, its SOAP fault tree, and the named types those trees use; optional keys are omitted when their value would be null, false or empty, except $maxOccurs, and keys are written in the order listed here, except in a type entry, whose description states its order

$schema.description: Relative path to this JSON Schema, which sits next to the generated files

tpgVersion.description: The Master's version attribute, or null when it has none

operations.description: Every operation of the Master, keyed by operation name in ordinal order

fault.description: The root elements of HdrFault, the element a SOAP fault's detail carries when a call fails, built like a response; null when the Master declares no HdrFault element

types.description: Every named schema type the element trees and the fault use, directly, through attributes or through base chains, keyed by local name in ordinal order

operation.description: One request message, its response message and the helpers derived from them

kind.description: The kind read from the operation-name suffix: Validate, Inq, Srch, Add or Mod, and other for anything else

requestElement.description: The global request element name, the root of the SOAP request body

responseElement.description: The global response element name, absent when the operation has no response

annotation.description: Documentation of the request element, or else of the request type

extendedElements.description: The x_ response elements a request can ask for through IncXtendElemArray, in ordinal order

records.description: Search operations only: the repeating response records in XSD order as paths from the response root joined with /, taken from the root and the level below it, or else the shallowest repeating elements anywhere in the response; a response root element named like a request root element is the request's criteria sent back and holds no records, and neither do x_ elements; absent when no record is found

modify.description: Modify operations only: how the request divides into changeable sections

items.description: One container and the sections that can be changed inside it

name.description: The container element name, or null when the sections sit directly under the request root

sections.description: The section element names in XSD order

request.description: The request's root elements, without message headers or version markers

response.description: The response's root elements, or null when the operation has no response

children.description: Elements keyed by name in XSD sequence order

node.description: One element, whose metadata keys start with $ and come first, followed by its child elements as ordinary keys in XSD sequence order

$type.description: The built-in XSD type name of the element's text content, such as string, date or decimal, absent for elements with child elements only

$typeName.description: The element's named schema type, a key of types, absent for anonymous and built-in types

$required.description: Request trees only: the element must appear whenever its parent does

$array.description: The element itself may occur more than once

$maxOccurs.description: Written exactly when $array is: the most occurrences allowed, or null when there is no limit

$recursive.description: The element's type is already being expanded higher up the tree, so its children are omitted

$attrs.description: The element's attribute names in ordinal order, described under the attributes of the type named by $typeName

$annotation.description: Documentation of the element, or else of the element it references, or else of its anonymous type

annotationFields.description: The documentation fields shared by annotations and type entries

description.description: The description text, with whitespace runs collapsed to single spaces

values.description: The canonical values, which on a type entry are the first non-empty value list along the base chain, starting with the type itself

deprecated.description: Present when the item is deprecated, even without a date or comment

date.description: The deprecation date as written in the schema

providers.description: Provider-specific documentation keyed by provider name in ordinal order

additionalProperties.description: One provider's non-empty fields keyed by child element name in ordinal order
The field text, with whitespace runs collapsed to single spaces

notes.description: Documentation fields other than the description, values, default and deprecation fields, inside Jx or as top-level elements without child elements, keyed by element name in ordinal order

additionalProperties.description: The field text, with whitespace runs collapsed to single spaces

typeEntry.description: One named schema type, shared by every element and attribute that uses it, whose documentation fields other than values describe the type alone without anything inherited; keys are written in the order base, baseTypeName, enum, values, description, default, deprecated, providers, notes, attributes

base.description: The built-in XSD type at the root of the base chain, absent for types with child elements only

baseTypeName.description: The nearest named base type, a key of types

enum.description: closed when values is the complete set of legal values, open when other values are allowed; only a closed list is safe to use as a closed union, and only for requests, and a closed entry can have no values, in which case clients treat it as a plain string

attributes.description: The type's attributes keyed by name in ordinal order

type.description: The built-in XSD type name of the attribute value

typeName.description: The attribute's named schema type, a key of types

required.description: The attribute is declared with use="required"
